annotations.description: Bottomed Bathe in Dragonfire (a strong removal spell) instead of a redundant Mountain, leaving a 6-card hand with 5 lands and only a 1/1 Blight Keeper as the sole spell. The hand is extremely land-flooded with almost no action.
annotations.actionTaken: Put Bathe in Dragonfire on the bottom of the library
annotations.betterLine: Put a Mountain on the bottom, keeping both Bathe in Dragonfire and Blight Keeper with 4 lands (Mountain, Mountain, Swamp, Thriving Moor) - a much more functional hand with removal and a 1-drop.

annotations.description: Playing Mountain instead of Swamp on turn 2 means the player cannot cast Blight Keeper this turn. With Swamp, they could deploy a 1/1 flyer immediately, gaining a turn of tempo. Mountain provides no useful play this turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Mountain as the first land, leaving no black mana to cast the 1-drop Blight Keeper.
annotations.betterLine: Play Swamp to have B available, then cast Blight Keeper this turn. Mountain or Thriving Moor can be played on subsequent turns.

annotations.description: The player timed out (no response) while attempting to cast Adventurous Impulse, which was rolled back. This resulted in doing nothing on turn 3 when they had 2 mana available. They could have cast Dragon Fodder ({1}{R}) to create two 1/1 Goblin tokens (which also sets up Volley Veteran synergy) or Adventurous Impulse to find a land/creature.
annotations.actionTaken: Attempted Adventurous Impulse but timed out, resulting in no action taken and wasting the entire turn's mana.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Dragon Fodder to create two 1/1 Goblin tokens, building board presence and setting up Volley Veteran's ETB trigger for later. Alternatively, successfully cast Adventurous Impulse to dig for a third land to curve into Fertilid or Dragon Fodder next turn.

annotations.description: Failed to play a land on turn 5 with only 2 lands on the battlefield, while holding 2 lands in hand and a hand full of 3-4+ mana spells (Domesticated Hydra, Fertilid, Dragon Fodder, Volley Veteran, Hunter's Edge). Missing this land drop delays the entire game plan significantly.
annotations.actionTaken: Timed out / no response, failing to play a land from hand.
annotations.betterLine: Play Forest (to have access to GG for Fertilid next turn, which would further ramp) or Mountain, then cast Dragon Fodder with the remaining 2 mana to start building board presence.

annotations.description: Playing Mountain instead of Forest reduces mana flexibility. With Mountain, next turn's lands are Forest+Mountain+Mountain, which cannot cast Fertilid (2G requires 2 green sources). Playing Forest first gives Forest+Forest+Mountain, enabling both Fertilid and Dragon Fodder next turn, while Mountain can be played the following turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Mountain from hand
annotations.betterLine: Play Forest to have 2 green sources next turn, enabling Fertilid (2G) as an option alongside Dragon Fodder

annotations.description: Activating Gnawing Zombie (presumably sacrificing Blight Keeper for a 1-life drain) before playing a land is suboptimal sequencing. Blight Keeper is a 1/1 flyer that can chip in damage each turn, and sacrificing it for just 1 life is a poor trade. The player should be developing their mana base to cast Tree of Perdition (4 mana) as soon as possible.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Gnawing Zombie before playing a land drop, sacrificing a flying creature for 1 life drain.
annotations.betterLine: Play Thriving Moor (choosing red) first to develop mana toward casting Tree of Perdition next turn, and keep Blight Keeper as a flying attacker for chip damage.

annotations.description: GLM47 spent all 4 mana on Domesticated Hydra (3/3) when they could have played Dragon Fodder (1R) + Fertilid (2G) in the same turn, deploying 4 total power across 3 bodies. This also sets up Volley Veteran to deal 3 damage on ETB next turn (2 Goblins + itself), which would cleanly kill the Gnawing Zombie. The Hydra's monstrosity ability is very expensive and unlikely to be relevant soon.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Domesticated Hydra for {2}{G}{G}, deploying a single 3/3.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Dragon Fodder ({1}{R}) + Fertilid ({2}{G}) to deploy 3 creatures with 4 total power, enabling Volley Veteran to ETB-kill the Gnawing Zombie next turn, and giving Fertilid's ramp ability for future turns.

annotations.description: GLM47 Timmy passed their entire precombat main phase with 4 untapped lands and multiple castable spells in hand (Dragon Fodder at 1R, Fertilid at 2G, Volley Veteran at 3R). They could have cast Dragon Fodder + Fertilid this turn to develop the board with three creatures, setting up Volley Veteran next turn to deal 3+ damage and kill Gnawing Zombie. Instead they did nothing, completely wasting a full turn's worth of mana.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without casting any spell, wasting 4 available mana and the entire turn.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Dragon Fodder (1R) to create two Goblin tokens, then cast Fertilid (2G) with remaining mana. This develops three creatures, enables Fertilid's land-searching ability for future turns, and sets up Volley Veteran next turn with 3 Goblins for a 3-damage ETB to kill Gnawing Zombie.

annotations.description: Activating Gnawing Zombie (sacrificing itself for 1 life drain) uses 1B of mana this turn, leaving insufficient mana to cast Tree of Perdition even after playing a land. Tree of Perdition is an extremely powerful card (0/13 that can exchange opponent's life total with its toughness), and delaying it by a full turn while also losing the only creature on board is a significant mistake.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Gnawing Zombie, sacrificing itself for 1 life drain, spending 1B mana.
annotations.betterLine: Play Swamp (or Thriving Moor), then cast Tree of Perdition for {3}{B} with the 4 available mana. Keep Gnawing Zombie as a blocker and future sacrifice outlet for Ruthless Disposal.

annotations.description: Activated Gnawing Zombie to sacrifice itself (the only creature on board) for a mere 1 life drain, instead of casting Tree of Perdition - an extremely powerful 0/13 defender that threatens to swap the opponent's life total to 13. Tree of Perdition was castable with the available 4 mana (2 Mountains + 2 Swamps = {3}{B}). Sacrificing the Gnawing Zombie also removes a creature that could have served as a sacrifice outlet or blocker, and wastes all mana that could have been spent on Tree of Perdition.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Gnawing Zombie, sacrificing itself for 1 life drain
annotations.betterLine: Cast Tree of Perdition for {3}{B}, deploying a 0/13 blocker that threatens to set the opponent's life total to 13 on the following turn

annotations.description: Playing Domesticated Hydra uses 4 mana to deploy a single 3/3, leaving 1 Mountain unused. The alternative of Fertilid (2G) + Dragon Fodder (1R) uses all 5 mana, deploys three bodies (2/2 + two 1/1s), provides future ramp via Fertilid's ability, and critically sets up Volley Veteran for next turn to enter dealing 2+ damage (with Goblins on board).
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Domesticated Hydra for a single 3/3 body, wasting 1 mana.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Fertilid (2G) then Dragon Fodder (1R) to deploy three creatures, use all mana efficiently, enable ramp, and set up Volley Veteran's Goblin synergy for the following turn.

annotations.description: Casting Volley Veteran with no other Goblins on the board means its ETB only deals 1 damage, which can't kill either Gnawing Zombie (1/3) or Tree of Perdition (0/13). Playing Dragon Fodder + Fertilid this turn (total 5 mana) would develop the board and set up Volley Veteran next turn to deal 3 damage (2 Goblin tokens + itself), enough to kill Gnawing Zombie.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Volley Veteran as the first creature, wasting most of its ETB damage potential (only 1 damage).
annotations.betterLine: Cast Dragon Fodder ({1}{R}) and Fertilid ({2}{G}) this turn to develop the board. Next turn, play Forest from hand and cast Volley Veteran for 3 damage ETB (3 Goblins), killing Gnawing Zombie.

annotations.description: Casting Exsanguinate before activating Tree of Perdition is a sequencing error. Tree swaps the opponent's life total with its toughness (13). If Tree activates first (opponent 17→13, Tree becomes 0/17), then Exsanguinate for X=2 puts opponent to 11. If Exsanguinate resolves first (opponent 17→15), then Tree swaps 15↔13, putting opponent to 13 and Tree to 0/15. The Tree-first line deals 2 more damage and leaves Tree with 2 more toughness for future exchanges.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Exsanguinate before activating Tree of Perdition
annotations.betterLine: Play Thriving Moor, activate Tree of Perdition (opponent 17→13, Tree becomes 0/17), then cast Exsanguinate for X=2 (opponent 13→11, you gain 2 life)

annotations.description: Targeted themselves with Gnawing Zombie's drain ability instead of the opponent. The ability reads 'Target player loses 1 life and you gain 1 life' - targeting yourself nets zero (lose 1, gain 1), while targeting the opponent would drain them for 1 and gain you 1 life, a 2-point life swing.
annotations.actionTaken: Targeted o3 Vorthos (self) with Gnawing Zombie's ability, resulting in net zero life change.
annotations.betterLine: Target GLM47 Timmy with the Gnawing Zombie ability to drain 1 life from the opponent and gain 1 life.

annotations.description: Casting Volley Veteran without first casting Dragon Fodder means Volley Veteran's ETB only deals 1 damage (counting itself) instead of 3 damage (2 Goblin tokens + itself). With 6 lands (4 Forest, 2 Mountain), both Dragon Fodder (1R) and Volley Veteran (3R) could be cast this turn. The extra 2 damage to Tree of Perdition (reducing it from 0/16 to 0/13 instead of 0/15) matters significantly against this threatening creature.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Volley Veteran first, dealing only 1 damage to Tree of Perdition with its ETB trigger.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Dragon Fodder first to create two Goblin tokens, then cast Volley Veteran to deal 3 damage to Tree of Perdition with its ETB trigger.

annotations.description: GLM47 timed out and passed their precombat main phase with 6 untapped lands and two castable creatures (Domesticated Hydra and Fertilid) in hand. This wastes an entire turn of development against a threatening board featuring Tree of Perdition. They also could have followed up with Dragon Fodder to start building toward their Goblin Grenade/Volley Veteran synergy.
annotations.actionTaken: Timed out, cast nothing with 6 available mana and two playable creatures.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Fertilid (2G) to develop the board and potentially ramp further, then cast Dragon Fodder (1R) with remaining mana to create two Goblins, setting up Volley Veteran and Goblin Grenade for the following turn.

annotations.description: Declined to activate Fertilid's ramp ability when it was the only available action and they have expensive cards in hand (Domesticated Hydra, Volley Veteran, Hunter's Edge). Getting an extra land would help deploy these threats faster. Fertilid is summoning sick so can't attack anyway, and the +1/+1 counter removal is a small cost given the mana acceleration benefit.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without activating Fertilid's land-search ability
annotations.betterLine: Activate Fertilid ({1}{G}, remove a +1/+1 counter) to search for a basic land, ramping from 7 to 8 lands for next turn to better deploy expensive hand cards

annotations.description: The opponent is at exactly 13 life. Casting Triskaidekaphobia (4 mana, easily castable) would threaten to kill the opponent at the next upkeep trigger if they can't change their life total. Instead, Exsanguinate for X=3 drops the opponent to 10 life, moving them OFF the critical 13 life threshold and wasting the Triskaidekaphobia combo. Tree of Perdition (currently 0/16) could later be used to reset the opponent to 13 or 16, but this requires extra steps.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Exsanguinate for X=3, dealing 3 damage and moving opponent from 13 to 10 life.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Triskaidekaphobia for {3}{B}. Opponent is already at 13 life and would lose the game at the next upkeep unless they can change their life total during their turn. Tree of Perdition stays untapped as a backup threat.

annotations.description: The opponent is at exactly 13 life with Triskaidekaphobia about to resolve as an enchantment. On o3 Vorthos's next upkeep, Triskaidekaphobia would trigger and the opponent at 13 life would lose the game. By activating Tree of Perdition, o3 Vorthos exchanged the opponent's 13 life with Tree's 16 toughness, moving the opponent to 16 life and completely negating the Triskaidekaphobia kill.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Tree of Perdition to exchange opponent's 13 life with Tree's 16 toughness, putting the opponent at 16 life.
annotations.betterLine: Do not activate Tree of Perdition. Let Triskaidekaphobia resolve, then on the next upkeep the opponent at 13 life loses the game immediately. The combo was already assembled without any further action needed.

annotations.description: GLM47 timed out and took no action in their precombat main phase with 7 mana available and 6 castable spells in hand. The opponent has the Tree of Perdition + Triskaidekaphobia combo threatening to kill them (Tree untaps next turn, swaps life to 13, Triskaidekaphobia kills at 13 life). Wasting this turn is potentially game-losing as it gives the opponent time to execute their combo without any board pressure or development from GLM47.
annotations.actionTaken: No response (timeout) — passed priority without casting anything despite having 7 mana and multiple strong plays available.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Dragon Fodder (2 mana) to create two Goblin tokens, then cast Volley Veteran (4 mana) dealing 3 damage to a creature (3 Goblins on board). This builds a threatening board with Goblin Grenade available next turn for 5 damage to the opponent's face, and creates pressure to race the combo. Alternatively, cast Domesticated Hydra as a strong body alongside Dragon Fodder.

annotations.description: Fertilid can attack for 1 damage completely unblocked — Tree of Perdition is tapped, there are no other creatures on opponent's side, and all opponent's lands are tapped. With Triskaidekaphobia on the battlefield making life totals critically important, every point of damage matters. There is zero risk to attacking.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to attack with Fertilid, passing combat with no attackers.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with Fertilid for 1 free damage, reducing opponent from 21 to 20. Every life point matters with Triskaidekaphobia in play.

annotations.description: The opponent has the Tree of Perdition + Triskaidekaphobia combo threatening lethal. Casting Domesticated Hydra does nothing to address this. With Dragon Fodder + Goblin Grenade targeting Tree of Perdition (5 damage, reducing it to 0/8), the combo becomes much less threatening. Adding Hunter's Edge (Fertilid fights Tree for 2 more, Tree to 0/6) uses all 7 mana and severely cripples the combo. Ignoring the combo is likely game-losing.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Domesticated Hydra, a vanilla 3/3 that doesn't address the lethal Tree of Perdition + Triskaidekaphobia combo.
annotations.betterLine: Dragon Fodder (1R) + Goblin Grenade targeting Tree of Perdition for 5 damage (R, sac goblin token) + Hunter's Edge putting counter on Fertilid to fight Tree for 2 more damage (3G). Uses all 7 mana, reduces Tree to 0/6, and severely weakens the combo while still having a goblin token and buffed Fertilid on board.

annotations.description: Failed to activate Fertilid's last +1/+1 counter ability to fetch a basic land. Fertilid as a 1/1 body is nearly irrelevant, and the extra land ramp would help power up Domesticated Hydra's monstrosity ability in future turns. With the Triskaidekaphobia/Tree of Perdition combo threatening, having more mana available is important.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without activating Fertilid, leaving its last counter unused.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Fertilid ({1}{G}, remove +1/+1 counter) to fetch a basic land onto the battlefield, ramping for future turns. The 1/1 body dying is essentially free since it provides negligible board presence.

annotations.description: Exsanguinate is unnecessary here. The Tree of Perdition + Triskaidekaphobia combo already provides a guaranteed kill: activate Tree to set opponent to 13 life, then Triskaidekaphobia kills them at the next upkeep. Casting Exsanguinate wastes a card that could serve as a backup win condition if something goes wrong.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Exsanguinate (draining opponent for some life before using the combo)
annotations.betterLine: Play Mountain, then simply activate Tree of Perdition to set opponent to 13 life. Save Exsanguinate as a backup win condition. Opponent dies to Triskaidekaphobia on next upkeep regardless.

annotations.description: GLM47 Timmy is at exactly 13 life with Triskaidekaphobia on the opponent's battlefield. On the opponent's next upkeep, Triskaidekaphobia will check and GLM47 will lose the game for having exactly 13 life. Playing Servant of the Scale does nothing to change their life total.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Servant of the Scale, which doesn't change life total and doesn't address the lethal Triskaidekaphobia trigger.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Goblin Grenade targeting yourself (going from 13 to 8 life) to move off exactly 13 life and survive the Triskaidekaphobia trigger. While painful, losing 5 life is far better than losing the game. Then continue developing the board with remaining mana.

annotations.description: GLM47 is at exactly 13 life with opponent's Triskaidekaphobia on board, meaning they will lose the game at the opponent's next upkeep. Hydra's Growth is a slow enchantment that provides no immediate impact. The player needs to either change their life total or attempt to win this turn. While winning this turn appears very difficult (only ~5 attack damage available plus Volley Veteran ETB vs opponent's 15 life), casting a slow aura guarantees wasting the mana on something irrelevant.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Hydra's Growth, a slow enchantment that won't help before dying to Triskaidekaphobia next upkeep.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Volley Veteran (to maximize board presence and ETB damage on Tree of Perdition), then attack with everything possible to push maximum damage. While likely not lethal, it at least gives more chances than a do-nothing enchantment. Alternatively, use Fertilid to search a land and thin deck, then cast the most impactful spell.

annotations.description: GLM47 Timmy was at exactly 13 life with Triskaidekaphobia's upkeep trigger on the stack. Letting it resolve (choosing the 'loses the game' mode) would have won the game immediately. Instead, o3 Vorthos activated Tree of Perdition in response, moving the opponent from 13 life to 15 life, removing them from the lethal 13 threshold before Triskaidekaphobia resolved.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Tree of Perdition in response to Triskaidekaphobia trigger, changing opponent's life from 13 to 15.
annotations.betterLine: Do not activate Tree of Perdition. Let Triskaidekaphobia resolve, choosing the mode where 'each player with exactly 13 life loses the game' — opponent at 13 life loses immediately.
